Scheduling & dispatch - AI tools for contractors

Booking jobs, routing crews, managing calendars and reducing no-shows.

Why this matters Double bookings and wasted drive time are the two most expensive scheduling mistakes.

What Scheduling & dispatch actually involves

Scheduling is the job that never appears on an invoice. Every hour lost to a badly routed crew or a technician sent to the wrong address is margin gone, and the cost stays invisible because nobody records it. Scheduling software starts paying for itself once you are running more than one crew and can no longer hold the week in your head.

Frequently asked questions

Which scheduling & dispatch tools are worth trying first?

The three that stand out here are Contractor Foreman (Small contractors who want one system instead of five spreadsheets), Housecall Pro (Home service businesses that want one app covering booking through to payment), Jobber (Owner-operators and small crews moving off paper and spreadsheets). Start with the one that matches your size and the work you do most, not the one with the longest feature list.

How much does scheduling & dispatch software cost?

Across the 9 tools on this page, 1 have a free tier and the rest are paid, most of them billed per user per month. Prices move often, so confirm on the vendor site before committing.

Can I try these tools for free?

Yes 鈥?Workiz all have a free tier, so you can run a few real jobs through them before paying anything.

Do I need scheduling software if I only have two vans?

Probably not yet. The pain usually starts around three or four people, when mistakes begin costing return visits. Below that a shared calendar is enough, and the money is better spent on getting paid faster.
